title: Tangzhong Grain & Seed Bread
description: A soft, generous loaf with the soul of old-world baking — built on modern tangzhong and a hearty, soaked grain-and-seed mix that gives depth without stealing moisture.

ingredients.item: water (adjusted to account for evaporation in tangzhong)

method.instruction: Make the tangzhong: In a small saucepan, combine 30g flour and 190g water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until it thickens into a paste (around 65°C). Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.

Prepare the seed and grain mix: Combine all seeds, grains, and add-ins (oats through soy lecithin) in a bowl. Cover with hot water and let soak for 20-30 minutes. Drain thoroughly and squeeze out excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine the 560g flour, salt, sugar, yeast, and bread improver (if using).
Add the cooled tangzhong, 180ml water, oil, and the drained seed mixture.
Mix until a rough dough forms. The dough will feel firm initially — this is normal.
Knead for 12-15 minutes by hand (or 8-10 minutes in a stand mixer) until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. It will relax and become more pliable as you knead.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and let rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours until doubled in size. The seeds make this dough denser, so it may rise more slowly.
Punch down the dough and shape into a loaf. Place in a greased loaf tin (approximately 20-22cm x 10-12cm).
Cover and let rise for another 60-90 minutes until the dough has risen about 2cm above the rim of the tin.
Optional: Brush the top with water or milk and sprinkle with extra seeds (oats, sesame, or sunflower).
Bake for 32-38 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
Remove from tin immediately and cool on a wire rack for at least 45 minutes before slicing. This allows the crumb to set properly.

notes.title: Why Soaking Matters
notes.content: The grain-and-seed mix is soaked because components like oats, bran, bulgur, freekeh, flax, chia, psyllium, and hemp absorb moisture. Soaking ensures the dough stays hydrated and the loaf rises tall with a tender crumb.

notes.title: Tangzhong + Seeds
notes.content: The tangzhong keeps the loaf soft for days, while the soaked seeds add hearty flavor and nutrition without weighing it down or stealing moisture from the dough.

notes.title: Customize Your Mix
notes.content: Don't have all the seeds? Use what you have. The total seed/grain weight should be around 145-150g. Popular combinations: oats + sunflower + pumpkin + flax + chia.
